name: impact-lens
description: Explore the potential impact of changing a function using VS Code language services.

commands.title: Impact Lens: Show Impact for Current Function
Impact Lens: Clear Live Change Session

impactLens.maxDepth.description: Maximum incoming-call depth used for impact analysis.

impactLens.maxNodes.description: Maximum number of symbols in one impact analysis.

impactLens.autoAnalyzeOnCursorChange.description: Automatically update impact information when the cursor enters another function.

impactLens.liveAnalysisEnabled.description: Reanalyze impact after unsaved source edits and show stale/analyzing/current states.

impactLens.liveAnalysisDebounceMs.description: Delay after the last source edit before live impact analysis starts.

impactLens.showCodeLens.description: Show function notes and Impact Lens actions above functions.

enumDescriptions: Show the result count, the traversal state and the semantic scope. Provider identity and reason codes stay in tooltips.
Also show the provider identity, its lifecycle stage and every coverage reason code in the visible header.
impactLens.provider.detailLevel.description: How much provider and coverage detail Impact Lens puts on the visible surfaces instead of tooltips.

impactLens.provider.doctorCommandLine.markdownDescription: Command line that **Impact Lens: Run Provider Doctor** offers to run in a terminal for the Agent CLI check. Running it is always your explicit choice: Impact Lens never runs it on its own and never reads its output. This setting can only be changed in your user settings, so a workspace you open cannot supply a command line for you. Leave empty to run host-side checks only.

enumDescriptions: Store new notes in VS Code workspace storage without changing project files.
Store new notes in .impact-lens/notes.json for version control and team sharing.
Store new notes as @impact-note comments in source files.
impactLens.defaultNoteStorage.description: Default storage option shown first when managing a function note.

scripts.test:all: npm run test:unit && npm run test:response-policy && npm run test:plugin-artifact
